$comment: HAND-EDITED source of the General section's own rows (cx-d5b5d): History, Window, Quitting, Columns (with column sizing and pane placement), the Sidebar group's workspace list rows, the Command Palette and Menus. scripts/cmux-next/gen-settings-sources.py writes the Swift descriptors and parser constants from it (its docstring is the full format, tabs.json's $comment the summary). SettingsSchema.all puts the Tabs rows (tabs.json) between window and quitting, so rows keep the export's order.

rows.note: Off: a command line can hold secrets, so recording commands is opt-in.

help.text: Lists finished shell commands in History. Command lines can contain secrets.
What Go Back and Go Forward walk: places in this workspace, in this window, or the focused page's own history.
Workspaces: Go Back and Go Forward move between workspaces and top pages, and return to the tab each one last had focused. Everything: they also step through tabs and panes inside a workspace.

summary.text: What Go Back and Go Forward step through

rows.name: commandRetention
rows.note: Whole days in the daemon's accepted range.

help.text: Each machine deletes recorded commands that are older.
Each machine deletes its oldest closed tabs, screens, workspaces and windows past this many. 0 keeps them all.
Each machine deletes closed items that are older. 0 keeps them however old they are.
Minimal has no titlebar strip; the top row moves the window.
With the sidebar hidden, On Hover hides the sidebar button, Back and Forward until the pointer is over the top row. With the sidebar open, they always show.
Show/Hide All Windows (⌃⌥⌘.) works while another app is in front.

summary.text: Show or hide all windows from any app

help.text: Start Agent (⌃⌥⌘Space) works while another app is in front. Change its key in Keyboard Shortcuts.

title.text: Hide Dock Icon When No Windows Are Open

help.text: cmux keeps running in the menu bar, out of the Dock and the app switcher, until a window opens.
A cmux item in the menu bar: open cmux, your account, working agents, help, Discord, updates, logs and Quit.
Terminals run in cmux-tui and keep running after cmux quits unless you end them.

rows.note: Lawrence 2026-11-10: an accidental Cmd-Q ended every agent and terminal with no question. Asks only when the quit ends them.

title.text: Ask Before Quitting Ends Agents or Terminals

help.text: Cmd-Q asks first when quitting would end working agents or open terminals. A quit that keeps the sessions running never asks.

rows.note: Two thirds of the viewport; the range is the daemon's column width range (set-viewport-pane-width).

help.text: A share of the window width, for Fixed Width new columns.
A thin bar under the columns that shows and moves the visible range.
Which pane gets focus when the focused pane closes.

lists.name: layout
lists.note: Split, new column, docked column, minimum pane size (plans/cmux-next/column-sizing.md) and new pane placement rows.

help.text: Even gives every pane in the column the same size after a split.

rows.note: Fixed at layout.defaultColumnWidth (two thirds): a new column is never full width just because the column beside it is (Lawrence 2026-10-28).

title.text: Top and Bottom Docks Full Width

help.text: Off hides New Row and fits a column's existing rows into it without scrolling.

summary.text: Rows of panes inside a column

rows.note: Off: hovering or scrolling a pane leaves keyboard focus where it is, so typing is never pulled into another pane.

help.text: Moving the pointer onto a pane or scrolling over it focuses that pane. Off keeps focus where you type until you click. Momentum and the first second after typing never move focus.

summary.text: Hovering or scrolling a pane focuses it

help.text: Side-by-side panes that do not fit scroll sideways instead of shrinking, also in docked columns.

rows.note: Command: Command + scroll moves the layout, a plain scroll goes to the pane under the pointer (Lawrence 2026-10-24).

help.text: Command + Scroll moves columns and rows from anywhere, and a plain scroll always scrolls the pane under the pointer. Without a modifier, a sideways scroll moves columns unless the pane scrolls sideways itself, and rows scroll only over the gaps between them.

summary.text: Command + Scroll moves columns and rows

rows.note: On: Figma and Excalidraw keep their Command + scroll zoom, every other page lets it pan the columns (Lawrence 2026-10-28).

title.text: Web Pages Get Command + Scroll First

help.text: A web page that uses Command + Scroll itself, such as Figma or Excalidraw zooming, keeps it. Over any other page, Command + Scroll moves columns. Off, Command + Scroll always moves columns.

summary.text: Figma and Excalidraw keep Command + Scroll zoom

help.text: Open a Tab adds a tab to the focused pane. Split Automatically splits the largest pane, like New Pane (Auto Layout).
With Split Automatically, new browsers also get their own pane instead of a tab.
Where a link or file you open from a terminal, an agent chat, Home or a page appears. Split Right uses the pane on the right, or makes one.
Agent Chats keeps an agent chat as the main pane: links, files, subagents and side chats it opens appear as tabs in a column on its right, and closing that column gives the chat its full width back.
Where Cmd-N, the + button and the CLI put a new workspace in the sidebar. A workspace made in a group goes to the same place inside that group. Pinned workspaces stay above it.
Off: one list of workspaces, and a workspace on another computer names it under its title. On: a section per computer.
A workspace you have not named shows its front tab's name: a page's title, an agent chat's title, or a terminal's title or folder. Your own name always wins.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope. A prefix you assign moves from any other scope.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope. A prefix you assign moves from any other scope.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope. A prefix you assign moves from any other scope.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope. A prefix you assign moves from any other scope.
Typed into an empty query, this character enters the scope. A prefix you assign moves from any other scope.
A word that names a command by its action id ("vs": "splitRight"). Typing the whole word in the command palette puts that command first.
Commands shown first when the command palette opens, in this order, by action id.

rows.note: On: the palette learns from what the person runs.

help.text: The row you pick for what you typed comes first the next time you type it, and rows you use often rank higher. Off, the palette records nothing and ranks by match and sidebar order only.
Adds Customize Menu… to the end of every right-click menu.

rows.page_hidden: Settings > Menus draws it as the first switch of its card
